Each section opens with the record's reproduction headline and any usage
warning ([label definitions](../eos-labels.md)), then the scope and basis of
the stored check. Only recorded content is shown: missing selections, weights,
errors or conventions are unknown, not zero, and are not inferred. Generating
this page fits nothing and changes no classification or source coefficient.
Every record is also listed by identifier in the
[numerical ledger](../primary-eos-refits.md#records), its
[machine-readable form](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/docs/data/primary-eos-refits.json) and the
[source-audit reports](../source-audits.md).

**Curves and residuals** replay the full stored source and reconstructed
coefficients on the same recorded audit inputs. Residual = model − input in
the fitted quantity's native units; for pressure, P(model) − P(input) at each
input volume and temperature (isothermal records use their reference
temperature). RMS is an unweighted descriptive error, not a parameter
uncertainty or the weighted fitting objective. With more than five
temperatures, the minimum, middle and maximum isotherms are drawn; residuals
include every selected row. Error bars appear only where all widths are
recoverable and keep the source meaning, including digitization widths.
No uncertainty band is inferred.

**Coefficient graphs** show stored central values and recorded error widths
in the audit's units; each panel includes zero. They are not observation or
residual plots. Fixed/adopted values are constraints, not recovered values.
Tables round an error to two significant digits when its leading digit is 1
or 2, otherwise one, and the value to the error's decimal place; values
without a positive error show at most six significant digits. Full precision
stays in EOSMAT and the ledger.

## Noguchi et al. (1999), shock BM3 isotherm

**close** · `nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_bm3_1` · `BM3` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/nickel_oxide.md#record-nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_bm3_1)

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** Every compared free coefficient meets either the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison or parameter-specific numerical similarity screen; the audit does not classify the complete comparison as parity.

- The reduction uses the source's Us=5.36+1.19up relation, 300 K Debye theta0=390 K, gamma0=1.38, gamma/V constant (q=1), and two atoms per NiO formula unit. The seven-state predecessor reproduces K0=184+/-5 GPa and about 1600 K at 132.9 GPa. The eight rounded journal rows recover the final coefficients within the residual-scaled refit errors; exact parity is unavailable because unrounded states, row-wise uncertainties, weights, and numerical objective are not published.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** nickel\_oxide\_noguchi\_1999\_table1\_shock
- **Observations:** 8
- **Fit kind:** shock\_to\_300k\_mie\_gruneisen\_debye\_then\_bm3
- **Selection:** all eight Table 1 final Hugoniot states; HEL precursor columns excluded; each pressure thermally reduced to 300 K before BM3 fitting
- **Objective:** unweighted\_reduced\_isothermal\_pressure\_residuals
- **Free parameters:** K0; K0\_prime
- **Fixed parameters:** V0

## Noguchi et al. (1999), derived B1 principal Hugoniot

**reproduced** · `nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2` · `LinearUsUpHugoniot` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/nickel_oxide.md#record-nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2)

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** nickel\_oxide\_noguchi\_1999\_table1\_shock
- **Observations:** 8
- **Fit kind:** linear\_us\_up\_hugoniot
- **Selection:** finite final\_particle\_velocity\_km\_s and final\_shock\_velocity\_km\_s; 8 rows
- **Objective:** shock\_velocity\_residuals
- **Absolute sigma:** False
- **Free parameters:** c0; s
- **Fixed parameters:** V0; rho0; P0

### Curves and residuals

![Source and refit curves with native-coordinate residuals for nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2](figures/nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2-curves.svg#only-light)
![Source and refit curves with native-coordinate residuals for nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2](figures/nickel_oxide_noguchi_1999_linear_hugoniot_2-curves-dark.svg#only-dark)

| Output / replay scope | Points | Residual units | Source RMS | Refit RMS |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Shock-velocity fit | 8 | km/s | 0.0556 | 0.0556 |

The fitted quantity is shock velocity, not isothermal pressure. Residual = Us(model) − Us(input). All selected final shock states are retained; HEL precursor columns are excluded. RMS is at observed particle velocities and can differ from an errors-in-variables latent-coordinate statistic. No P–V branch extrapolation is used.
